species.look_here_first: Follow a low leafy shoot to a tiny flower head. Check opposite hairy leaves, then examine the overlapping bracts beneath the head and the barbed awns on mature fruits.
morphology_keys: Low perennial with opposite, toothed, simple leaves.
Small heads combine ray and disk florets.
Mature flattened fruits bear unequal, barbed awns.
photo_roles: Whole creeping shoot and an attached opposite leaf pair.
Head from above and below with millimeter scale.
Mature fruits showing the unequal awns under magnification.
species.lookalike_work: Compare low lawn Asteraceae using head underside and mature fruits; exact local confuser key remains pending. Small yellow flowers alone are insufficient.

species.look_here_first: Start at the basal clump of narrow, keeled leaves and follow the flowering stalk upward. Photograph a six-parted flower and the three-chambered fruit rather than relying on flower color.
morphology_keys: Bulb-forming perennial with basal linear leaves.
Flowers occur along an elongated raceme.
Six spreading floral segments surround the stamens.
Fruit is a three-chambered capsule.
photo_roles: Basal leaves and complete flowering stalk.
Flower front and side showing six floral segments.
Mature capsule with scale and, if already open, chambers.
species.lookalike_work: Regional comparison with death-camas and other bulbous monocots is required before a confident species key. This draft provides no edible-use advice.

species.look_here_first: Find a fruiting stem with flattened, triangular to heart-shaped pods on slender stalks. Confirm the basal rosette, clasping stem leaves and four-petaled flowers.
morphology_keys: Annual with a basal rosette before stem elongation.
Stem leaves are alternate and clasp the stem.
Small flowers have four petals.
Flat pods have two chambers.
photo_roles: Fruiting branch with attached mature pods.
Basal rosette and a stem-leaf base.
Flower macro and opened pod with scale.
species.lookalike_work: Vegetative rosettes overlap other mustards. Close Capsella relatives require a regional floral/fruit key; a heart-shaped pod alone is not independent exact-species verification.

species.look_here_first: Inspect the leaf hairs with magnification: they branch like small stars. Pair this with mostly opposite, shallowly lobed leaves and tiny flower clusters in the leaf axils.
morphology_keys: Weak-stemmed annual with trailing or rising shoots.
Long-stalked leaves are mostly opposite and palmately lobed.
Star-shaped hairs occur on shoots and leaves.
Tiny axillary umbels produce dry fruits splitting into two one-seeded halves.
photo_roles: Node showing leaf arrangement and axillary flower cluster.
Leaf-surface macro resolving the branched hairs.
Mature two-part fruit with millimeter scale.
species.lookalike_work: Compare small lobed-leaf herbs using hair form, leaf attachment and fruit. Do not identify only from groundcover appearance; exact local confuser comparison remains pending.

species.look_here_first: Photograph a complete compound leaf attached to the twig, then examine a mature husk and nut. Leaflet count helps, but the fruit and twig are needed for a reliable hickory comparison.
morphology_keys: Deciduous tree with alternate pinnately compound leaves.
Leaves typically have 7–17 finely toothed, lance-shaped leaflets.
Mature husks split along four seams.
Older bark forms flaky plates.
photo_roles: Whole compound leaf and twig attachment.
Leaflet underside with veins and hairs.
Mature attached husk, nut and twig buds with scale.
species.lookalike_work: Compare with pecan and other hickories using mature nut/husk, buds and leaflet details; habitat or leaflet count alone cannot distinguish them.

species.look_here_first: Check the large heart-shaped leaves and long narrow seed capsules, then photograph the lowest corolla lobe. Its shape helps distinguish southern from northern catalpa.
morphology_keys: Deciduous tree with opposite or whorled simple leaves.
Flowers have a bell-shaped corolla with internal markings.
Long capsules split lengthwise to release winged seeds.
photo_roles: Twig showing leaf arrangement and leaf base.
Flower front resolving the lowest corolla lobe.
Attached capsule and seed wings with scale.
species.lookalike_work: NC State describes an undivided lower corolla lobe for C. bignonioides versus a cleft lobe in C. speciosa. Confirm multiple characters and the exact source plant; color and flowering dates alone are insufficient.
